# iliad-016 (3.1–83) — review

Reviewer pass 1 (units.json, new-renderings.md) and pass 2 (gloss.json, read against the lines and against known-forms.json). `t` was not touched: the `t` of all 44 units is byte-identical before and after (checked by script). All edits were made by script. Severity: high = a rendering or claim that misleads the reader about the Greek; medium = a false grammatical label, a departure from a house rendering, or a rendering that mis-binds the Greek; low = wording, precision, or consistency.

Totals: high 0 · medium 16 (11 in units.json, 5 in gloss.json) · low 20 (17 in units.json, 3 in gloss.json). Refused: 14 (below). Scansion flags: none in the packet; see the last section.

## Other file touched

`new-renderings.md`: the τίσεσθαι, 3.76 and 3.83 rows brought into line with the edits above; one row added for κλαγγῇ τ’ ἐνοπῇ τ’ (ἐνοπή “shouting”, which differs from the Odyssey table’s “a voice” at 10.147, a different use) so that the departure is recorded.

## Findings considered and refused

1. 3.1 `i` “in the open sky” for οὐρανόθι πρό: “open” is not in the Greek, but the note says that the English renders the pair and the sense of the phrase is not settled; kept.
2. 3.10 `i` ends with a colon where `l` has a semicolon: both are acceptable for the ano teleia before ὣς; kept.
3. 3.25 `i` “devours it greedily” for μάλα: a slight colouring of ‘very much’; kept as ordinary intensifying English (`l` has “greatly”).
4. 3.43 `i` “Surely” without “I suppose” (ἦ που): the note gives both; kept.
5. 3.8 “might” (μένεα, table) and 3.45 “might” (ἀλκή, table): two Greek words, one English, but each is the table’s own rendering; kept.
6. 3.45 “force” (βίη) and 3.62 `i` “force” (ἐρωή; `l` “rush”): no table row for ἐρωή; the `l` keeps them apart; kept.
7. 3.21 note: σῶμα “in Homer is a dead body”, and 3.4 note on the Pygmies at war with the cranes: lexical or explanatory statements the line itself supports; kept.
8. 3.35 note refers to the Odyssey line: iliad-001 does the same; kept. `l` and the first clause of `i` are verbatim those of odyssey-088 as the packet requires.
9. 3.60 note’s closing clause (“the sharper the axe, the more the man’s effort tells”): interpretation, labelled as such, harmless; kept.
10. 3.12 τόσσόν printed with two accents: that is the source’s text and `t` is not touched.
11. 3.18 δηϊοτῆτι called ‘epic’ in the gloss: the word itself is Homeric (no Attic δηϊοτής); kept.
12. 3.12 and 3.33 `i` shifts the aorists of the similes to the present: each unit’s note says so; kept.
13. 3.39 `i` “fairest in looks” for εἶδος ἄριστε (`l` “best in form”): `i` is allowed to be freer; kept.
14. Quotation marks, `mark`, `p`, `ln`: checked and correct — “ opens the first unit of Hector’s speech (39) and ” closes its last (56–57 unit); likewise Alexander 59–75 and Agamemnon 82–83; `mark` on 39, 59, 82; `p` on 1, 10, 15, 21, 30, 38, 58, 76 as the packet’s ¶; every `l` has the same number of lines as its `t`, no `i` contains a newline, no ASCII quotes. The speech at 38 is introduced with a colon and has no quotation mark on the introducing unit, as it should. The previous part (iliad-015) ends the Catalogue and runs no speech into this one; iliad-017 is not drafted, and 3.83 closes Agamemnon’s speech.

## Scansion

The packet flags no line. I ran the Odyssey’s scanner over every line of the part: no line is UNRESOLVED. It reports ordinary licences (correption, hiatus at a pause, position by digamma, a short syllable in the arsis at a caesura or pause); the costliest lines are 3.18 (κεκορυθμένα) and 3.25 (initial μάλα), which the scanner fits only with metrical lengthening of those words’ syllables. I judged them regular Homeric scansions of those words, not irregular lines, and added no note. No unit’s note was changed for metre.
